question: Can the internal status report (D01) be relied upon for the 11:00 external review of release 3.2?
situation_summary: D01 reports release 3.2 as Green and Confirmed for go-live on 17 March. Supporting records only partly back this up. 'Confirmed' is defined differently across teams, the staging contract tests for billing API v2 were skipped (D03), and a TLS certificate expiring on 20 March has no clear internal owner (D06). On current records, D01 can be used externally only with qualifications.
overall_assessment: Usable only with caveats: 'Confirmed' and 'Green' in D01 do not meet the Delivery definitions required for external reporting (D05).

claims.text: D01 reports overall status Green and release 3.2 as Confirmed for go-live on 17 March, with no High risks open.
Engineering marked the billing API v2 integration as confirmed because PR #482 was merged with unit tests passing.
qualifications: D02 notes that contract tests against the customer sandbox were still scheduled to run overnight.

claims.text: The Confirmed status for the billing integration in D01 likely reflects Engineering's definition (code merged), not Delivery's definition for external reporting (verified end-to-end in staging and signed off by QA).

conflicts.note: 'Confirmed' = code merged with unit tests (Engineering) vs. verified end-to-end in staging and signed off by QA (Delivery).

qualifications: Inference: D01 does not state which definition was used; PMO's glossary defines Confirmed as reported done by the team lead.

claims.text: The nightly pipeline for rc4 (06:05) shows PASSED overall, but staging-contract-tests was SKIPPED because the staging environment was locked by a manual performance test.

conflicts.note: D01 lists the integration as Confirmed, while the pipeline stage that verifies it did not run.

claims.text: The payment-gateway TLS certificate expires on 20 March. Renewal requires a signed CSR from the customer, and internal ownership is unclear.
qualifications: D04 was last updated 15 days ago (24 Feb).
D06 is a partial chat export: 2 replies are missing.

claims.text: D01 rates risk R-14 (TLS certificate) as Low and handled by Infrastructure, which conflicts with D06. Under D05, an unowned go-live risk should be rated at least Medium.

conflicts.note: 'Handled by Infrastructure' (D01) vs. customer action needed and internal owner unclear (D06).

projections.outcome: If the staging contract tests pass before 12 March, UAT can start on schedule and go-live on 17 March remains achievable.
assumptions: The billing integration works against the customer sandbox (unverified: D03 stage skipped).
Valid v2 sandbox credentials are installed in staging (last recorded status 'pending', D04, 24 Feb).

projections.outcome: If the payment-gateway TLS certificate is renewed before 20 March, card payments continue working at and after go-live.
assumptions: The customer signs the CSR in time.
An internal owner is assigned to follow up.

limitations.description: No record shows staging contract tests passing for any 3.2 release candidate.
No record newer than 24 Feb states the status of the v2 sandbox credentials.
'Confirmed' has different definitions in Engineering (D02) and Delivery (D05); D01 does not state which one applies.
Internal ownership of the TLS certificate renewal is unclear since the previous security contact left. The chat export is incomplete.
Only the PMO coordinator can confirm which definition of Confirmed was used when compiling D01.

The Confirmed status for the billing integration in D01 likely reflects Engineering's definition (code merged), not Delivery's definition for external reporting (verified end-to-end in staging and signed off by QA).
The nightly pipeline for rc4 (06:05) shows PASSED overall, but staging-contract-tests was SKIPPED because the staging environment was locked by a manual performance test.
The payment-gateway TLS certificate expires on 20 March. Renewal requires a signed CSR from the customer, and internal ownership is unclear.
D01 rates risk R-14 (TLS certificate) as Low and handled by Infrastructure, which conflicts with D06. Under D05, an unowned go-live risk should be rated at least Medium.

competing_hypotheses.explanation: D01 is accurate in substance: the integration works and only the formal staging run is pending.
competing_hypotheses.what_would_resolve: A completed staging contract-test run against the customer sandbox.

competing_hypotheses.explanation: D01 overstates readiness: 'Confirmed' reflects only the code merge, and end-to-end integration is unverified.
against: No record shows a test failure yet
competing_hypotheses.what_would_resolve: Contract-test results or confirmation from the PMO coordinator.

revisions.stopping_reason: Concluded after 8 of 8 tool calls: all six available records were read. Remaining open points require confirmation from people rather than records.
